findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the sqlExpressions toggle a no-op
findings.body: The function reads `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, but both control-flow branches return false, so SQL expressions are rejected regardless of whether the feature toggle is enabled. This makes the still-existing `sqlExpressions` feature flag a no-op and leaves the `QueryTypeSQL` parsing branch below unreachable. If disabling is intentional, it should be explicit (for example `return false` with a comment), or the toggle/docs should be updated; otherwise the dead flag and unreachable code create a misleading contract and a future risk of accidental re-enable.

findings.title: No regression test covers that SQL expressions are disabled
findings.body: The PR changes behavior for all SQL expression queries but includes no tests asserting the new rejection behavior. There should be a regression test for `ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` returning an error, and for `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand` rejecting SQL commands without doing any DuckDB work, so this security fix cannot be accidentally reverted by future refactors.
